# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 28 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 28 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_028_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 2, continued — Further on Simplicity

**1** I said, "Sir, I have a question." "Ask it," he replied. "If someone in need receives help but turns out to be a hypocrite, and the giver did not know — is the giver condemned for it?" **2** He replied, "The giver who gives without knowing is innocent; but the one who received in hypocrisy will pay a penalty." **3** "The one who gives simply to whoever is in need, without making distinctions, acts rightly. The judgment falls on the deceiver. The giver has fulfilled his ministry before God." **4** "But I have heard some people say, 'I give to no one, for fear of giving to a hypocrite.' What is your answer to that?" He replied: **5** "All things are known to God. Therefore do not hesitate when you see someone in need. Give — because you are responding to what is visible to you; it is not for you to know what is in the heart, for only God knows that. Those who receive deceptively will deceive other people, but they cannot deceive God. Such a person will answer for their deception. **6** The one who gives is righteous, because he has fulfilled the commandment of the Lord — to give to all who are in need. He will be blessed and will live to God."

---

*LOGOS note: The Shepherd here explicitly addresses a real pastoral objection — the reluctance to give for fear of being deceived. The theological resolution is elegant: God knows all hearts; the giver acts on visible need and is answerable only for that.*
